message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75 (filled at $222.75, ~$9,801 total), staying within the mandate's $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps and using a limit essentially at the market (quote: last $222.70, bid $222.68 / ask $222.72). The fundamentals supported a buy: Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth quarter (ended Sept 28, 2024) showed revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and for the full fiscal year the 10-K filed 2024-11-01 reported revenue of $391,035M, net income of $93,736M, diluted EPS of $6.08 (including a one-time $10.2B tax charge), and operating cash flow of $118,254M — a business still growing with very strong cash generation. News flow was neutral-to-mildly-positive (iPhone 16 demand and Apple Intelligence rollout being weighed by investors), so I sized the position modestly rather than aggressively. One caution worth flagging: a search result claimed AAPL was halted all day under "rule T12," but that claim came from a single unofficial-looking site (nasdaq-halts.net) and was directly contradicted by the broker's live two-sided quote, so I treated it as unreliable rather than acting on it — the order executed normally. I did not touch the existing 100 MSFT shares and moved no money out of the account.
